source.title: Tripwire: Triggering Aligned Refusal via Statistically Certified Safety Neurons
source.authors: Wei Zhao; Zhe Li; Pei-Xin Zhang; Jun Sun

page_placements.theme: Small selected neuron sets causally control or predict specific behaviours beyond random controls

record.tranche_reason: The study uses identified neurons as units for a jailbreak defense and reports defense performance. It does not test whether neurons have one or a few interpretable jobs, whether explanations predict unseen activations, or whether neuron-based attribution graphs explain model behavior.
record.gate_note: The reported experiments evaluate TripWire's safety-neuron clamp as a defense. They do not measure the interpretability or explanatory fidelity named by the claim versions. The paper also cites results from NeuroStrike and other work; those cited results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses statistically selected MLP neurons as units for a jailbreak defense. It reports only attack success rate, MT-Bench utility, over-refusal and overhead. It never measures how many neurons have one or two interpretable jobs, whether explanations predict activations, or whether neuron graphs explain behaviour.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. More precisely, the authors conclude that utility costs of neuron-level defenses come from fixable design problems, not neuron granularity. These problems are erasure-style blocking, classifier-based attribution and always-on intervention. They report that FDR-controlled selection plus a trigger-style clamp gives ASR at most 2.0% with the smallest utility drop among defenses.
record.recipe_differences: The paper identifies safety-related neurons using per-neuron statistical tests and a utility-specificity filter, then clamps or edits them for jailbreak defense. It does not use the claim's proposed neuron-pole job audit or test explanations on held-out activations.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports different outcomes by model, neuron budget, and deployment form; it does not report these as changes in neuron interpretability or explanation fidelity.

fits_no_version.finding: Clamping the top-2500 FDR-filtered safety neurons (top-5000 for Qwen2.5-32B) at harmful-conditional means cuts average ASR from 17–43% to at most 2.0% across four models and four attacks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Clamping statistically selected safety neurons reduces jailbreak success in the tested models.

fits_no_version.finding: In inference mode, MT-Bench utility drops 0.5–5.3% on three models; the always-on edit form costs more (up to about 27% on Llama-3.1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A neuron-level safety clamp has limited utility cost when detector-gated, but larger cost when always on.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the aggregate results in the text. The study evaluates defense and MT-Bench utility, not the interpretability claims at issue.
record.rows_left_out: Defense results in Table 1 and the ablation results in Table 2 are not separately recorded because they measure TripWire's defense performance, not any claim version's interpretability or explanation-prediction outcome.

untested.parts: All: share of neuron poles with one job, two related jobs, or unknown jobs in Qwen3-32B.
All: interpretability shares across models, dense and MoE, and scale.
All: InceptionV1 polysemantic examples, pose, recursive generalization.
All: architecture, regularization and tools as causes of messy neurons; tool-driven rise in interpretable share.
All: neuron attribution graphs explaining behaviour without replacement models.
All: whether activating-example explanations predict firing on new inputs.

record.verdict_notes: The paper assumes some neurons are safety-specific and admits some serve both safety and general functions. It never measures the share of single-job neurons or validates any neuron explanation, so nothing bears on V1–V7. The Figure 3 layer distribution of selected neurons is a selection property, not a claim result.

versions.untested_parts: The share of neuron poles with one job, two related jobs, or jobs not yet understood.
Interpretability shares across models, architectures, and scales.
The InceptionV1 cat-and-car example, pose, and recursive generalization.
Whether architecture, regularization, or tools explain interpretability differences, including the stated InceptionV1-sized estimates.
Attribution graphs, explanation of behavior, trained replacement models, and reconstruction error.
Whether explanations based on activating examples predict firing on unseen examples.
Automated explanation scores based on simulated activations on new text.

rows.note: Aggregate defense result for TripWire, not a measure of how many neurons have a single interpretable job or whether neuron explanations predict activations.
rows.check: This is the study's own method compared with baselines, not a claim measure; keep only as a fits_no_version finding. The baseline is stated in Table 1: undefended average ASR is 43.0%, 33.1%, 24.1% and 17.2%. 'At most 2.0%' holds for the large-budget inference form; the large-budget edit form is also at most 1.7%.

source_check.correct: Baseline stated: undefended average ASR 43.0% (Llama-2-7B), 33.1% (Llama-3.1-8B), 24.1% (Qwen2.5-7B), 17.2% (Qwen2.5-32B). The at-most-2.0% value holds at top-2500 (top-5000 for Qwen2.5-32B) in both inference and edit forms. It does not hold at top-2000 for Qwen2.5-32B, where ASR is 5.9% (inference) and 5.6% (edit); top-2000 is the scaled small budget.

rows.check: The 0.5%–5.3% drop applies only to the large-budget inference form on Llama-2, Llama-3.1 and Qwen2.5-7B. In the edit form, MT-Bench falls further (e.g., Llama-3.1 from 6.60 to 4.84, about 27%). The row should state the deployment form and models. It is also the study's own method's performance, not a claim measure.

source_check.correct: The 0.5%-5.3% range is for the inference-based (detector-gated) form at top-2500, stated for Llama-2 (5.3%), Llama-3.1 (4.7%) and Qwen2.5-7B (0.5%). Table 1 Qwen2.5-32B top-5000: 8.23 to 8.14 (about 1.1%). Edit form top-2500: Llama-2 4.94 to 4.31, Llama-3.1 6.60 to 4.84, Qwen2.5-7B 7.40 to 5.86, Qwen2.5-32B 8.23 to 7.45 (drops of about 9.5-27%).
